run.question:
Alertmanager alert PendingPodsDetected (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/otel-demo since 2026-11-18T01:46:27Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The PendingPodsDetected alert (current: 2) is explained by two pods that cannot be scheduled in namespace otel-demo: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh. Both are new-replica pods created at 01:45:30Z and 01:45:38Z by the new ReplicaSets ad-dd7f45975 and cart-5b597c6db5, owned by Deployments ad and cart respectively. The scheduler reports '0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector', and both pending pods carry spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"} while no node in the cluster has that hostname label (the five nodes are i-01a47734339426210, i-037e40963128cbd9f, i-0424ef08cd107882f, i-08831c4b8af18ed15, i-097278082719f10ba). The source of that selector is the pod template of Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart (deployment revision 2, progressing since 01:45:30Z/01:45:38Z); these are the only two of the 21 otel-demo deployments whose template sets a nodeSelector, and no ConfigMap in the cluster contains the value invalid-node. Resource shortage, image pull failure and the flagd fault flags are rejected as causes. What applied the invalid selector at ~01:45:30Z could not be identified: change history is not integrated and the Helm/CI record is not readable, so the conclusion is partial. Observed service impact was limited to the unschedulable new replicas: the old pods ad-554b849958-42mdm and cart-755465879b-bgb2p remained Ready and are the sole endpoints of Services ad and cart, and ad/cart span throughput stayed flat across 01:25-02:00Z.

claims.text: Cluster-wide exactly two pods are in Pending phase, both in namespace otel-demo: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh, each with nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node and PodScheduled=False reason Unschedulable; this matches the alert annotation 'current: 2'.

Warning events FailedScheduling from default-scheduler at 01:45:30Z (ad-dd7f45975-mw86p, count 3 through 01:55:53Z) and 01:45:38Z (cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh, count 3 through 01:55:53Z) state '0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/5 nodes are available: 5 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

Both pending pods have spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"}, no affinity, only the two standard not-ready/unreachable tolerations, no nodeName and status condition PodScheduled=False/Unschedulable with lastTransitionTime 01:45:30Z and 01:45:38Z.

None of the five cluster nodes carries kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node; their hostnames are i-01a47734339426210 (control-plane taint), i-037e40963128cbd9f, i-0424ef08cd107882f, i-08831c4b8af18ed15 and i-097278082719f10ba, so the selector matches no node.

Deployment otel-demo/ad has spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"}, generation 2, annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2, Progressing condition (ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975 is progressing) last updated 01:45:30Z, and status replicas 2, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1; Deployment otel-demo/cart has the same invalid-node nodeSelector in its pod template and 1 ready/available replica.

Among the 21 deployments in namespace otel-demo, only ad and cart set a pod-template nodeSelector (kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node); all other deployments (accounting, checkout, currency, email, flagd, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, postgresql, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart) have none.

Ownership chain: new ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975 (spec.replicas 1, no ready/available) is owned by Deployment ad and created pod ad-dd7f45975-mw86p; new ReplicaSet cart-5b597c6db5 (spec.replicas 1, no ready/available) is owned by Deployment cart and created pod cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh; the previous ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and cart-755465879b still each have 1 ready and 1 available replica.

Deployment events show the rollout that produced the pending pods: 'Scaled up replica set ad-dd7f45975 from 0 to 1' on Deployment ad and 'Creating pod: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p' at 01:45:30Z, and 'Scaled up replica set cart-5b597c6db5 from 0 to 1' on Deployment cart with 'Created pod: cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh' at 01:45:38Z — about one minute before the alert started at 01:46:27Z.

Services ad and cart still have exactly one ready endpoint each (ad -> ad-554b849958-42mdm at 100.96.3.180 on node i-037e40963128cbd9f; cart -> cart-755465879b-bgb2p at 100.96.3.205 on the same node), i.e. the pending pods are not endpoints.

Span throughput of the two owners did not drop across 01:25-02:00Z: 10-minute span increases stayed roughly flat (ad ~950-1180, cart ~8300-10600 spans per bucket), so traffic continued while the new replicas were unschedulable.

The only error-status span series returned for ad/cart in the 01:10-02:01Z window is service ad: its increase of STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans was 0 in the 01:25 and 01:30 buckets and ~1.05 per 10 minutes from the 01:35 bucket onward, i.e. it began before the 01:45:30Z rollout; a sampled ad error span is operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream (duration 600016224 us, rpc.grpc.status_code 4, started 01:23:56Z) with a visible child flagd span. No cart error series was returned, so cart's error status is unknown rather than zero.

The flagd-config ConfigMap's flags all have defaultVariant "off" (including adFailure, cartFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, imageSlowLoad, emailMemoryLeak, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable), and none of them governs pod scheduling.

Insufficient node CPU/memory (resource pressure) is not the reason the two pods are pending: the scheduler message attributes 4 of 5 nodes to 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' and 1 to the control-plane taint, and both pods request only 10m CPU / 225Mi memory with PodScheduled=False/Unschedulable rather than any resource-fit failure.

Image-pull failure or container crash (ImagePullBackOff/CrashLoopBackOff/OOMKilled) is not the cause of these pending pods: neither pod has a nodeName, startTime or container statuses, and the only Warning events for them are FailedScheduling at the scheduler stage.

The ad trace errors seen in the window are not the cause of the pending pods and are not tied to the 01:45 rollout: they are 600-second flagd EventStream spans with gRPC status 4 that start 01:23:56Z and produce a steady ~1 error span per 10 minutes from 01:35Z, i.e. before the deployment change, while ad/cart span volume stayed flat.

The fault originates in the pod templates of Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart, which both carry nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node (revision 2) and therefore keep producing unschedulable replicas; because two distinct Deployment objects hold the same invalid setting, the single applying object could not be identified from the available data.

A Helm release update of release otel-demo in namespace otel-demo (both deployments are labelled app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=Helm with annotation meta.helm.sh/release-name=otel-demo and are at deployment revision 2) is the plausible mechanism by which the invalid node selector reached both pod templates at ~01:45:30Z; the release record itself (stored in Secrets) could not be read, so this remains unverified.

Remove or correct the nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node from the pod templates of Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart (or roll them back to the prior revision/values) so the new ReplicaSets ad-dd7f45975 and cart-5b597c6db5 can schedule, and confirm the change source (Helm release otel-demo / CI values) before re-applying.

gaps: No change-history integration is available, so what applied nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node to Deployments ad and cart at ~01:45:30Z/01:45:38Z (a controller, CI job or human edit) could not be observed; the Helm release record lives in Secrets, which cannot be read.

Queries for mutatingwebhookconfigurations and validatingwebhookconfigurations returned status error (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so an admission webhook that could have injected the node selector was not checked.

Prometheus returned no kube_* series at all (get_metric_names for {__name__=~"kube_deployment.*"}, {__name__=~"kube_pod.*"} and {__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned no_data) and the alerting rule PendingPodsDetected was not listed, so the alert's own expression and current pod/deployment counts could not be verified from Prometheus; the pending count of 2 rests on the Kubernetes API view at 02:01Z and the alert annotation.

A metrics_range_query for kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="otel-demo",deployment=~"ad|cart"} returned no_data, so no kube-state-metrics timeline of availability exists in this target.

The error-log queries on ad-554b849958-42mdm and cart-755465879b-bgb2p over 01:30-02:01Z returned no matching error lines (status no_data); this is not proof that those containers logged no errors, and cart's error status is unknown because no cart STATUS_CODE_ERROR series was returned.

Cart's deployment status detail (unavailableReplicas) and the old ReplicaSets' pod restart counts were only partially read; no container termination reasons exist for the pending pods because they never started.
next_steps: Inspect the Helm release history / CI pipeline for release otel-demo in namespace otel-demo to identify when and why the nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node was added to the ad and cart values, and revert it.
Review admission controllers (mutating/validating webhooks) once the API read succeeds, to rule out automatic injection of the invalid node selector.
Verify the PendingPodsDetected alerting rule and its kube-state-metrics source, which were not present in this Prometheus target, and confirm the pending count there once the schedule is fixed.
